resource.title: CS 4727/5727 Adversarial Machine Learning（Alex Vakanski, Boise State，讲稿 ppt/pdf 全公开）
resource.covers: 课程页把每讲讲稿（ppt + pdf）挂在网上，页面还给出往季（2023/2024/2025）存档：Introduction to Adversarial Machine Learning、Deep Learning Overview、Mathematics for Machine Learning、White-box Evasion Attacks、Black-box Evasion Attacks、Introduction to Large Language Models、Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models、Defenses Against Evasion Attacks、Poisoning Attacks and Defenses、Adversarial ML in Cybersecurity（Network Intrusion Detection / Malware Detection and Classification / Spam Filtering, URL Detection, and Cyber-physical Systems）、Privacy Attacks and Defenses、Explainability in ML、Bias and Fairness in ML。对应节点的攻击面与威胁模型、对抗样本（白盒/黑盒 evasion）、数据投毒、隐私攻击、LLM 越狱与模型应用防护（defenses/robust ML），并且明确把攻击与防御落到网络安全场景（入侵检测、恶意软件分类器、垃圾邮件），正好接上节点的「与网络空间安全交叉」。

courses.prereq_text: Prerequisites: CS 2120 Practical Python, or CS 4771 Python for Machine Learning, or Instructor Permission. Students are expected to have a basic understanding of linear algebra, probability and statistics, and machine learning concepts. Familiarity with neural networks and deep learning is recommended, but not required. A working knowledge of Python programming is required to complete the course.

prerequisites: The main prerequisite is either CIS 5200 (Machine Learning), or CIS 4190/5190 (Applied Machine Learning) AND CIS 3333 (Mathematics of Machine Learning). The course requires both mathematical maturity, including experience with mathematical proofs, and familiarity with machine learning libraries.

extra_prereqs.evidence: Boise CS 4727/5727 'A working knowledge of Python programming is required to complete the course'（先修课 CS 2120 Practical Python / CS 4771）。
Boise CS 4727/5727 'basic understanding of linear algebra, probability and statistics, and machine learning concepts'。
Boise CS 4727/5727 要求机器学习概念；Penn CIS 4270/5270 的主先修是 CIS 5200（Machine Learning）或 CIS 4190/5190 + CIS 3333。
Boise CS 4727/5727 'Familiarity with neural networks and deep learning is recommended, but not required'。
Penn CIS 4270/5270 原文 'including experience with mathematical proofs'（鲁棒性验证那一讲要用）。

notes: 原图对本节点没给建议前置（candidate_check 为空），课程证据反而显示它建立在机器学习基础之上（Boise 要 ML 概念、Penn 要一门 ML 课），并推荐但非必须深度学习；所以从证据看 A.2.1 应当是它的前置，A.2.3 可作为 recommended。资源选 Boise 这门课而不是 NIST 报告：它是可直接学的课程（逐讲讲稿），覆盖面正好对齐「攻击面→对抗样本→投毒→滥用/越狱→防护→安全交叉场景」。权威框架建议配套 NIST AI 100-2e2023《Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations》（https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-2e2023.pdf ，已抓取正文核实：按攻击者目标/能力/生命周期建 taxonomy，覆盖 evasion、data poisoning、privacy breach 与对应 mitigations，并讨论 LLM/chatbot）——用来给节点里的「攻击面/威胁建模/滥用评估」提供统一术语。未核实的部分：本节点简介里的「模型应用防护」若指 LLM 应用层防护（prompt injection、输出过滤），这次没有核实 OWASP 之类的清单页面，不作引用。
